children: The UAE-based Mashreqbank, rated A (Fitch), A3 (Moody’s) and A (S&P), all with a stable outlook, has mandated a five-year dollar-denominated Regulation S senior unsecured bond.

ADCB, ANZ, Barclays, BBVA, BofA Securities, Emirates NBD Capital, First Abu Dhabi Bank, ICBC, Mashreq, MUFG, Societe Generale and Standard Chartered Bank have been mandated to arrange a series of fixed income investor calls on Tuesday 8 September.
The drawdown issuance will come under Mashreq’s $5 billion Euro Medium Term Note Programme, subject to market conditions.

Since late August, a slew of debt issuances has kicked off in the GCC after a brief slowdown in capital markets following an escalation in regional tensions between Iran and the US. In recent weeks, Saudi Arabia banks, including Al Rajhi and Arab National Bank have raised debt, along with the kingdom raising $3.25 billion last week through a sovereign sukuk. Similarly, Kuwaiti lenders have also gone to market with issuances by Kuwait International Bank and Boubyan Bank.
(Writing by Bindu Rai, editing by Seban Scaria)

title: UAE’s Mashreqbank mandates 5-year benchmark USD bond
